acceptanceCovered: next/image accepts a Google OAuth avatar URL from public.users.avatar_url on every site that renders it
a host absent from the allowlist is still rejected, and dangerouslyAllowLocalIP stays false for any public/hosted Supabase hostname
the pattern list is covered by unit tests that assert through Next's own hasRemoteMatch matcher and fail if the Google patterns are removed
next.config.ts is proven to actually ship the pattern list, not merely to have it available
typecheck, lint at --max-warnings 0, format:check, the full unit suite and its 100% coverage gate, and the production build all pass
regressionChecked: Supabase Storage kudo attachments (kudos-image-strip.tsx) still match via the unchanged resolveSupabasePattern branch
dangerouslyAllowLocalIP IPv6 loopback branch now actually fires (bracket-stripping fix) instead of silently never matching
dangerouslyAllowLocalIP still false for hosted Supabase and unaffected by the new avatar patterns

the three other avatar render sites (kudos-sunner-options.tsx, kudos-card-person.tsx, kudos-leaderboard.tsx via build-gift-recipient-items.ts) consume the same shared remotePatterns list, so the fix is not profile-hero-only
story fixture no longer depends on a third-party host (i.pravatar.cc) that was never allowlisted

findings.summary: Completeness claim ('no app path writes avatar_url, so this list is complete') is true for src/ code paths but the column is directly writable: migration 0001_users_table.sql:47-51 grants an own-row UPDATE RLS policy and :59 grants column-level UPDATE(avatar_url) to authenticated. A user calling supabase-js directly (bypassing all src/ code) can set avatar_url to any string. remotePatterns still blocks the fetch (no SSRF widening), but it reintroduces the exact 'Invalid src prop' render crash for any other Sunner who views that profile/card, and no error.tsx/global-error.tsx exists anywhere under src/app to contain it.

src/configs/ is a brand-new top-level directory sitting alongside the existing src/constants/; no doc in ./docs prescribes where a Next-config-only module belongs, so this is a defensible but unreviewed convention choice worth a one-line mention next time docs/system-architecture.md is touched.
